Delgado Community College.basis: Delgado's published dual enrollment program requirements (2026-2027), which restate Board of Regents Academic Affairs Policy 2.22 for courses on the Articulation Matrix and set the college's own floor for technical courses.
Delgado Community College.gradeLevelNote: Sophomores may be eligible in some instances. Parental permission and school administration permission are required, and the student must be in good standing at the high school.
Delgado Community College.sourceName: Delgado Community College, Dual Enrollment page

University of Louisiana at Lafayette.basis: UL Lafayette University Connection dual enrollment criteria, revised February 13, 2026. The university catalog states an added ACT composite of 21 for the program; the program's own criteria page does not list a composite, so this check follows the program page and says so.
University of Louisiana at Lafayette.gradeLevelNote: Students must be at least 15, enrolled in a Louisiana high school or approved homeschool, on track for the TOPS core, in good standing, with scores and an official high school transcript on file. Juniors take courses on their high school campus only; seniors may also take courses at UL Lafayette. A student may enroll in at most 7 credit hours per semester.
University of Louisiana at Lafayette.sourceName: UL Lafayette University Connection, High School Dual Enrollment Criteria

english.label: ACT English 18 (for humanities and social sciences courses)

math.label: ACT Math 19 (for math and science courses)

University of New Orleans.basis: Board of Regents Academic Affairs Policy 2.22 state minimums for academic dual enrollment. UNO's own added criteria, if any, are not yet in this data, so a passing result here means the state floor is met, not that UNO has admitted the student.
University of New Orleans.gradeLevelNote: UNO runs a dual enrollment program with its own application cycle (a spring application deadline of November 15 is published to counselors). Confirm UNO's own requirements on its admissions pages.
University of New Orleans.sourceName: Louisiana Board of Regents, Academic Affairs Policy 2.22 (dual enrollment minimum eligibility)

policyNote: Louisiana Board of Regents Academic Affairs Policy 2.22 sets the statewide floor: for academic dual enrollment courses, a 2.5 cumulative high school GPA with either subject minimum scores or a counselor recommendation, a 3.0 subject-area GPA with counselor recommendation, a 2.5 college GPA from earlier dual enrollment, or an approved Early College Academy's thresholds. Colleges may add their own criteria on top of the floor, and UL Lafayette does.
